title: Carpet Cleaning CRM: 7 Tools to Win Repeat Customers
html:
A carpet cleaning CRM stores every customer, reminds you to follow up and brings past customers back. Start with the free HubSpot CRM or the client tools inside a job app such as Jobber or Kickserv. Published plans here run from $0 to $199 a month.

Carpet cleaning lives on repeat work. A customer cleaned this spring is the easiest sale you will make next spring. A CRM is the list that makes that second sale happen without a cold call.

This guide sorts seven tools by what they do for customer follow-up. Every price comes from the vendor page linked beside it, read in November 2026, and each tool gets one real limit.

Which carpet cleaning CRM is free or low cost to start?

The HubSpot free CRM is the lowest-cost start, and Kickserv Start is a low-cost job app with built-in reminders. Both store customers, but only one tracks jobs.

  • HubSpot CRM: the free plan covers up to 2 users and 1,000 contacts with no time limit. The paid Starter plan is listed at $20 per seat a month, with new-customer pricing of $7 billed annually or $10 billed monthly. Starter adds automation and meeting scheduling. Limit: the free plan caps contacts at 1,000 and email sends at 2,000 a month with HubSpot branding.
  • Kickserv: Start is $60 a month for 5 users and lists an embeddable contact form, automated email and text reminders and QuickBooks Online integration. Run is $119 for 10 users and adds custom data fields. Limit: the page does not list scheduling or invoicing as plan features, so confirm what is included.

A free CRM is a good first step for a company with a few hundred customers. A carpet cleaner with 1,500 past customers will pass the free contact cap, so plan for that before you import.

Contact forms close the loop. A form on your site that drops each request straight into the list means no one retypes a phone number from a voicemail. Kickserv lists an embeddable contact form on Start, so ask other vendors for the same.

A general CRM does not know about rooms, stains or van routes. You can add custom fields for room count and last service date, but the job record lives in another tool. That split is the main cost of a free CRM.

Clean the list before you import it. Merge duplicates, fix phone formats and delete customers who asked to be removed. Ten minutes of cleanup now saves you from texting the same person twice later.

Keep the import simple. Name, phone, email, address, last service date and rooms cleaned are enough to start. Extra columns that nobody fills in turn a clean list into a messy one.

Which job apps double as a carpet cleaning CRM?

Jobber, Housecall Pro and Service Fusion all keep a customer record next to the job. For most carpet companies, that beats a separate CRM because the history builds as you work.

  • Jobber: customizable client profiles, job history, a communication history of emails and texts, and tags that mark contacts as leads. Core for one user is $49 a month with no commitment. Connect adds automated reminders at $139 for one user billed monthly with no commitment. Limit: extra users are $29 a month each.
  • Housecall Pro: online booking, scheduling, estimates, invoicing and review management on Basic. Basic is $79 a month billed monthly or $59 billed annually for one user. Limit: add-ons such as Campaigns and Pipeline are listed without prices.
  • Service Fusion: customer management, estimates and jobs, scheduling and integrated payments with unlimited users. Starter is $208 a month billed annually, and plans are month to month. Limit: the Customer Web Portal is an add-on on Starter, and no price is shown.
ToolCRM features named on the vendor pageEntry price shownUsers
HubSpot free CRMContacts, pipelines, email tools$0Up to 2
Jobber CoreClient details, job history, lead tags$49 monthly, $29 billed annually1
Kickserv StartContact form, reminders$60 monthly5
Housecall Pro BasicBooking, estimates, review management$79 monthly, $59 billed annually1
Service Fusion StarterCustomer management, scheduling$208 billed annuallyUnlimited

Published list prices from each vendor page, November 2026. Taxes, add-ons and card fees are extra.

Communication history is the feature to test first. When a customer calls about last month's job, you want the text thread and the invoice on one screen. Jobber lists a record of emails and texts, which is exactly that.

Notes need structure. Free-text notes such as dog barks or key under mat are useful on the day, but they are hard to search. Use a custom field for the facts you will filter on, such as pet in the home or stairs count.

Lead tags matter too. A quote request that has not booked yet is a lead, not a customer. Jobber lists tags that mark contacts as leads, so open quotes do not hide among finished jobs.

Which CRM tools automate follow-up and campaigns for carpet cleaners?

Workiz and Jobber Grow automate follow-up, and both cost more than a plain customer list. Use them once you have a rebooking routine worth automating.

A simple rebooking routine beats a clever one. Send a reminder at the interval you recommend, such as six or twelve months after the last clean. Include the rooms cleaned last time and a link to book.

Test every automation on yourself first. Add your own phone number as a customer and run the reminder end to end. Many owners find a wrong name or a broken link only after fifty customers have received it.

Segment by service. A customer who bought pet odor treatment gets a different note than one who cleaned a living room. Even two segments, standard clean and add-on buyers, make the message feel less like a blast.

Seasonal timing helps the routine. Many homeowners think about carpets before guests arrive or after a long winter. A reminder sent a few weeks ahead of those moments reaches people who are already planning a clean.

Keep texts short and permission-based. Ask at booking whether the customer agrees to texts, and record the answer in the CRM. Check the rules that apply in your state before you send campaigns.

What does a carpet cleaning CRM cost each month?

A free CRM costs $0, and a job app with built-in follow-up lands between $49 and $199. These totals add plan fees only, so card fees and taxes come on top.

SetupPartsMonthly plan cost
Free startHubSpot free CRM, Google Business Profile$0
Job app with client recordsJobber Core billed monthly with no commitment$49
Low-seat job app with remindersKickserv Start billed monthly$60
Automated follow-upJobber Grow for one user billed monthly with no commitment$199

Built from the vendor prices above, November 2026. Annual billing lowers several figures but ties you to a year.

Watch the seat count as you grow. HubSpot free stops at 2 users, Jobber charges $29 a month for each extra user, and Kickserv Start stops at 5 users. A CRM that is cheap for an owner can get pricey once two office staff and four techs need logins.

Divide the cost by repeat jobs, not by all jobs. If a $49 CRM brings back ten customers a month, each return costs under $5 in software. If it brings back none, the plan is the wrong tool or the routine is missing.

Decide who owns the list. In a small company it is usually the owner or one office person. Without a named owner, reminders slip, and a CRM nobody checks is just a second place to lose customers.

Track one number: the share of customers who book a second clean within your chosen interval. Check it every quarter. That figure tells you whether the CRM is earning its monthly price.

How do you choose a carpet cleaning CRM?

Choose a carpet cleaning CRM with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it keep rooms cleaned and last service date per customer, send reminders by text and email, and tag open quotes as leads?

Cost: add the plan price, extra seats, add-ons and card fees, then divide by your repeat jobs per month.

Setup effort: can you import your customer list and build one reminder in a weekend?

Ask for a data export before you commit. Your customer list is the most valuable asset the tool holds. If you cannot download it as a spreadsheet, switching later gets expensive, and you stay with a tool you may have outgrown.

A one-van owner should start with the HubSpot free CRM or Jobber Core. That is the whole stack. Add automation once a manual rebooking routine works and takes too much time.

A multi-van company fits Jobber Grow or Workiz, with a clear owner for the list. Test on one segment, such as last spring customers, before you message everyone.

A CRM only keeps customers, so pair it with lead sources. Ads from carpet cleaning Google Ads and rankings from carpet cleaning SEO bring new homeowners in. The carpet cleaning advertising guide covers where to spend first.

What is the best CRM for a carpet cleaning business?

There is no single best tool, because it depends on how many customers you keep and who sends the follow-ups. The HubSpot free CRM suits a small list. Jobber and Kickserv keep customers beside jobs. Workiz and Jobber Grow add automation. Test one on a real customer list.

How much does a carpet cleaning CRM cost?

Published prices in this guide run from $0 for the HubSpot free CRM to $199 a month for Jobber Grow billed monthly with no commitment. Jobber Core is $49 a month and Kickserv Start is $60. Card fees, extra seats and add-ons cost more.

What should a new carpet cleaning company set up first?

Claim a free Google Business Profile, then keep every customer in one list from day one. Start with the HubSpot free CRM or one job app on a free trial. Add reminders next, then campaigns. Skip paid automation until the manual routine works.
